prompt: Determining the scope of distribution for a restaurant-equipment manufacturer involves deciding
choices: how many warehouses will be needed and where they will be located.
how much stock to keep on hand without being overstocked.
whether to use a direct or indirect channel of distribution.
how widely the manufacturer's products should be distributed.
explanation: How widely the manufacturer's products should be distributed. The restaurant-equipment manufacturer could decide to use intensive, selective, or exclusive distribution. Deciding whether to use a direct or indirect channel of distribution pertains to selection of the channel of distribution. Deciding how many warehouses will be needed and where they will be located relates to warehouse decisions that managers must make. Determining how much stock to keep on hand to satisfy customers without being overstocked pertains to the level of stock that a business should maintain.

prompt: A business that has the capability of monitoring the location of delivery trucks to determine if a full-service restaurant's shipment is on time is using the technology of
explanation: Satellite tracking. Satellite tracking technology is based on the use of orbiting satellites and enables businesses to monitor the location of delivery trucks. Once a full-service restaurant's shipment is placed on a truck, the shipment can be tracked by satellite so businesses know where the shipment is at all times. This technology makes it possible for businesses to tell customers exactly where the shipment is and when it will be delivered. Artificial intelligence is technology that is used to make computers perform functions that people perform. Data interchange involves the exchange of information between one business's computer system and another business's computer system. Electronic imaging makes it possible for businesses to scan or take electronic photographs of documents.

prompt: Preventing other full-service restaurant distributors from obtaining and selling the same product to customers is an example of a(n) __________ that is illegal.
explanation: Tying agreement. A tying contract, or agreement, is an illegal agreement requiring a customer to buy other products in order to obtain desired goods and services. Tying agreements are considered illegal if they substantially limit competition by preventing other distributors from obtaining and selling the same product to customers. An exclusive dealing arrangement between a supplier and an intermediary states that the intermediary will distribute only that supplier's products and will not handle a competitor's products. A strategic alliance is a long-term relationship between two or more businesses. A marketing plan is a set of procedures or strategies for attracting the target customer to a business.

prompt: What is a full-service restaurant doing when it makes sure enough ingredients to prepare a menu item that the restaurant is heavily advertising on television?
choices: Developing a relationship with a vendor
explanation: Coordinating distribution with promotion. Full-service restaurants coordinate distribution with their promotional activities to make sure that sufficient quantities of menu items are available when they are advertising them. If a business plans to promote a certain menu item or offer it at a special sale, the full-service restaurant must make sure that an adequate supply of ingredients will be on hand to prepare the item so the restaurant can meet consumer demand. Full-service businesses may lose customers if they advertise items that are not available because they failed to make the necessary distribution plans. A full-service restaurant is not arranging a method of transportation, developing a relationship with a vendor, or communicating information about a product when it makes sure a sufficient supply of ingredients are available to prepare menu items for an advertised sale.

prompt: Which of the following is a criterion that some full-service restaurant chains might use to evaluate channel members:
explanation: Return policy. Full-service restaurant chains usually evaluate channel members on a regular basis to make sure that they are performing as expected. In order to evaluate performance, the full-service restaurant chains develop criteria such as return policies. This criterion is important to full-service restaurant chains that want to be able to return products for agreed-upon reasons. If full-service restaurant chains find that channel members are not meeting these standards, they often work with the channel members to improve performance. If channel members continue to perform in an unacceptable manner, they may be terminated. Businesses usually are not concerned with shipping method, management style, or marketing plan as long as the channel members meet certain criteria and perform effectively.

prompt: When you state a fact, it's important to
explanation: Be accurate. When you state a fact, it's important to be accurate. Make sure you can support your statement. Don't generalize. Stating a fact is not usually about thinking before you speak (as in stating an opinion) or about changing your mind (as in hearing a fact stated by another person).

prompt: Which of the following would be an effective way to communicate a job-related suggestion to your supervisor:
explanation: An office memorandum. An office memorandum, or memo, is the most commonly used method of in-house communication in many businesses. It may be handwritten, typed, or sent by e-mail. A letter of transmittal is a letter that accompanies a long report or proposal. A business letter would be used to communicate with another business. It is inappropriate to write a personal letter to a supervisor.

prompt: An important guideline for full-service restaurant managers to follow when conducting staff meetings is to
explanation: Begin and end on time. When conducting staff meetings in a full-service restaurant, it is important to begin on time rather than wait for employees who are late. If you wait, it sends the message that it is acceptable to be late, and more employees might start showing up late. Also, it is important to end on time. Full-service restaurant employees are usually busy getting ready for the peak serving period and do not have time to wait on employees who are late. If the agenda states that the meeting will last one hour, then it should end in an hour. Important or priority issues should be discussed first. The leader should not dominate the group but control the staff meeting so all of the full-service restaurant's employees have an opportunity to participate. The manager or meeting leader should control the talkative member but not try to silence that person.

prompt: What is the first step that full-service restaurant employees should take in handling customer complaints?
choices: Ask the customer for a solution.
Determine the appropriate action to take.
explanation: Listen to the customer. The customer should be allowed to explain the entire complaint before anything else is done. In some cases, it is helpful to restate the complaint to ensure understanding. The customer may ask for a specific resolution to the problem, such as returning a cold entree to the kitchen so it can be reheated. Or, the full-service restaurant employee might ask the customer what s/he would like to have done. Determining the appropriate action to take cannot be done until the complaint has been clarified.

prompt: Employees who are unable to respond to questions about the restaurant-supply company's goods or services can affect the customer's
explanation: Image of the business. Customers form an image of a restaurant supply business as they communicate with employees. When employees cannot answer questions, customers receive a negative impression. The customer's purchasing ability is determined by the amount of his/her disposable income or budget. The customer's sourcing strategies are generally determined independent of a specific employee interaction. Price fixing is an illegal activity in which a business charges different prices for similar amounts and types of products.

prompt: If a restaurant-supply company receives only standard merchandise in cartons, each containing a dozen items, the most efficient method of checking a shipment would be a(n) __________ check.
explanation: Spot. A spot check involves a random check of part of the shipment rather than a check of each item or container. Since each carton is marked by the manufacturer as to content and count, spot checking should suffice. Merchandise that is varied by size, color, etc., requires a direct check in which the goods are checked directly against the purchase order or invoice. A blind check is a listing of goods received on a blank form, or dummy invoice, which is then compared to the real invoice.

prompt: One reason full-service restaurants regularly pick up debris off the floor and remove trash and empty boxes is to
choices: keep the work area free from hazards.
explanation: Keep the work area free from hazards. Debris, trash, and empty boxes on the floor are a hazard in the work area because employees and customers might trip and fall. Keeping the area clean and free from potential hazards is a way to prevent accidents and avoid injuries. Most full-service restaurants do not pick up debris and trash to meet community insurance standards, to provide employees with additional duties, or to create additional storage space.

prompt: A full-service restaurant received a shipment of defective tablecloths. Stephanie is responsible for sending items back to the vendor. Which of the following forms may need to be sent with the tablecloths:
explanation: A claim form. When shipments are lost or arrive damaged, a claim is filed by the purchaser to obtain credit or reimbursement. The return amount is filed against the vendor or the carrier depending on who is responsible for the damage. A receiving log is used to record all shipments, while an inventory report is a record used to list all goods on hand. A shipping report shows the transportation method used and date of delivery.

prompt: Which of the following is a reason why restaurant-supply businesses might buy and store larger amounts of stainless steel pans than they need:
explanation: To obtain special discounts. Some restaurant-supply businesses buy larger amounts of goods than they need because the price is very attractive at that time. They may want to take advantage of special discounts by buying in bulk or in the off-season. Restaurant-supply businesses do not buy more than they need in order to spend operating capital, to reduce profit margins, or to increase interest payments.

prompt: Which of the following do full-service restaurants consider when planning the arrangement of storage space:
explanation: Accessibility. The layout of storage space is an important factor because full-service restaurant employees should be able to easily access the areas to obtain needed food items and supplies. Restaurants usually try to arrange storage space so food items are located near the kitchen area but away from chemicals and cleaning supplies to prevent contamination. During peak dining periods, it is necessary for employees to be able to get replacement food items from storage areas as quickly as possible in order to serve customers promptly. Privacy, territoriality, and atmosphere are considerations when planning the layout of the front of the restaurant.

prompt: In a restaurant-supply business, which of the following is often a function of a computerized inventory records system:
explanation: Automatic reorder. Modern restaurant-supply businesses often maintain inventory records in computerized systems that enable the restaurant-supply businesses to constantly monitor the level of inventory. A function of a computerized inventory system often is to automatically reorder goods when a specified level of supply is reached. Automatic reordering allows restaurant-supply businesses to maintain inventory at an adequate level at all times. Computerized inventory systems do not set prices, select vendors, or pay invoices.

prompt: An economic risk that most restaurant suppliers must take into consideration involves
explanation: Changes in consumer demand. A common economic risk involves shifts in consumer demand. When consumers' needs and wants change, their demand for products change also. Items that are hot sellers one season might not be in demand the next season. Restaurant suppliers try to predict changes in consumer demand in order to avoid or reduce economic risk. Unfavorable weather conditions are natural risks. Careless employee behavior and the spreading of false rumors are human risks.

prompt: What is one reason that certain natural resources are sometimes in short supply?
explanation: Weather conditions. The supply of some natural resources is affected by weather conditions and the natural environments in which the resources exist. The availability of many crops is often affected by weather conditions that are too cold, too wet, too hot, or too dry. Demographic changes refer to the availability of human resources. Scientific advances often help to increase the supply of certain natural resources. Local traditions refer to the particular customs of an area.

prompt: Which of the following demonstrates the interrelationship among primary business activities:
choices: A new product is introduced, so business advertisements must adjust in response.
A business changes its goals, so its strategies and tactics change too.
One business activity changes, so the others must adjust in response.
A business manager becomes vice president, so his/her department must adjust to the change.
explanation: One business activity changes, so the others must adjust in response. Since the primary business activities are interrelated, when one business activity changes, the others must adjust in response. Changes in the products introduced, changes in specific employee roles, and changes in business strategies/tactics do not represent the interrelationship of business activities overall. They represent smaller changes that take place within specific business activities.

prompt: Why does the government set and collect taxes?
choices: To help businesses grow and prosper
To increase the use of technology
To help pay the expenses of government
explanation: To help pay the expenses of government. One of government's main sources of revenue is taxes, which are collected from businesses and individuals. Businesses pay several types of taxes including sales, excise, income, and property taxes. Increasing technology, providing economic security, and helping businesses grow and prosper can be goals of a political party or government administration, but are not reasons that the government sets and collects taxes.

prompt: What usually results when interest rates continue to increase?
explanation: Spending decreases. The interest is money payments for the use of borrowed money. When the interest rate increases, such as from 6% to 10%, the cost of borrowing money increases. Therefore, a lot of businesses and consumers decrease spending, especially for expensive items that they pay for with credit. High interest rates have a negative impact on the economy because decreased spending leads to a decrease in production, a decrease in purchasing power, and an increase in unemployment.

prompt: When a recession continues, many businesses fail, and people lose their jobs; a(n) __________ exists.
explanation: Depression. A severe, long-lasting recession characterized by high rates of unemployment and business failures is a depression. A depression exists if a severe recession lasts for more than six consecutive months. Expansion is the first stage of the business cycle, characterized by increased spending and borrowing, increased demand for goods and services, increased employment rates, and decreased interest rates on loans. Trough is the fourth phase of the business cycle, which is considered the low point of economic activity. Contraction is the third phase of the business cycle, characterized by decreased demand for goods and services, rising unemployment, increased saving by consumers, and reduced sales and profits for businesses.

prompt: A restaurant-supply business that obtains private information about a customer's financial status and makes that information public is behaving in an __________ manner.
explanation: Unethical. Most restaurant-supply businesses gather a wide variety of information about their customers that often includes their financial status and credit rating. How restaurant-supply businesses use this information or provide it to others is a matter of ethics, which are the basic principles that govern behavior. Customers have the right to assume that the financial or private information they provide to a restaurant-supply business will remain confidential. If a restaurant-supply business violates that confidence and makes private financial information available to the public, it is behaving in an unethical manner. Although disclosing private financial information is unethical, it is not immoral or impersonal. Such practices are not illegal at present; however, legislation governing this type of behavior is possible for the future.

prompt: Which of the following approaches would help full-service restaurant employees involved in conflict to negotiate a solution to the problem that is satisfactory to all:
explanation: Being willing to compromise. Some kind of compromise is necessary to the solution of most conflicts. Individuals seeking to resolve the conflict need to be open-minded and willing to make concessions in order to find a solution that everyone involved can accept. Being determined to win at all costs, using aggressive tactics, and trying to manipulate others in the group are negative approaches that are more likely to hinder resolution of the conflict than to resolve it.

prompt: Leaders who share a belief in justice, a desire to do the right thing, and an awareness of the rights of other people can be said to have
explanation: Integrity. People with integrity adhere to an established set of personal ethics and sound moral principles. Leaders tend to share a belief in justice, a desire to do the right thing, and an awareness of the rights of other people. Competence, emotional intelligence, and credibility are other, separate leadership activities. Competence is the ability to do what needs to be done. Emotional intelligence is the ability to recognize and manage emotions in ourselves and in others. Credibility is how much people believe what you say.

prompt: A manager of a photography studio believes employees work better together and become more motivated when they are included in the decision-making process. This manager prefers a(n) __________ management style.
explanation: Democratic. Democratic-style managers seek input from employees and discuss work-related problems with them. Authoritarian managers emphasize assigning specific job duties and responsibilities with little employee involvement. Laissez-faire is an open style in which managers provide little or no employee direction.

prompt: Full-service restaurant chains follow the generally accepted accounting principles (GAAP) because the principles help communicate financial information in a(n) __________ way.
explanation: Consistent. Generally accepted accounting principles (GAAP) are universal rules that accountants use when they prepare and summarize financial reports. By using the same standards and rules, accountants prepare the reports in a consistent way, so the information is clear to all people who read and work with financial information. Accountants do not follow GAAP to communicate information in an uncooperative, biased, or adaptable way.

prompt: If a full-service restaurant forecasts that it will seat 65 of its 85 available tables in the next hour, what will be the restaurant's table-seating percentage?
explanation: 76%. Forecasting the percent of sales is important for many businesses. For example, restaurants might forecast sales based on the percentage of available tables. To determine the percentage, divide the number of tables that can be seated by the total number of tables available (65 ÷ 85 = .76 or 76%).

prompt: How much is a full-service restaurant supplier's net profit if its sales are $819.50, cost of goods is $625.00, and operating expenses are $67.50?
explanation: $127.00. Net profit is the money remaining after operating expenses are subtracted from gross profit, the difference between the cost and the selling price. Thus, by subtracting the cost and the operating expenses from the selling price, the net profit is determined ($625.00 + $67.50 = $692.50; $819.50 - $692.50 = $127.00).

prompt: A full-service restaurant chain that currently has 200 employees plans to expand and hire 15 more employees next year. If the full-service restaurant chain also expects to lose 12% of its employees to retirement and terminations, how many new employees will it need to hire next year?
explanation: 39. Full-service restaurant chains consider the number of new employees they plan to add as well as the number that will leave when determining future hiring needs. In this example, the full-service restaurant chain expects to lose 12% of its employees and plans to hire 15 additional employees due to expansion. To calculate the number of new employees it will need to hire next year, first determine the number of current employees who will leave (200 x 12% or .12 = 24). The full-service restaurant expects to lose 24 employees and wants to add 15 new employees for a total of 39 (24 + 15 = 39).

prompt: Which of the following activities typically occurs during new employee orientation at a full-service restaurant:
explanation: A tour of the business. New employee orientation usually includes activities that will provide new employees with information about the full-service restaurant. Orientation also helps to put new employees at ease and helps to eliminate many of their anxieties about their new surroundings. Reviewing the employee's résumé and contacting the employee's references are usually done before the business hires the employee. A performance appraisal is a tool that evaluates how well the employee performs his/her job duties. Employees receive performance appraisals after they have worked for a certain amount of time.

prompt: In addition to competence level, which of the following should full-service restaurant workers be able to increase as a result of participating in a training program:
explanation: Productivity. Training programs are conducted in an effort to improve workers' skills and, thus, increase productivity. Unless the training program dealt with development of delegation skills, workers' abilities in these areas would not be affected. The salary of a full-service restaurant employee will not necessarily increase because of participation in a training program. The well-trained worker should become more independent, rather than dependent.

prompt: Workers who feel they are treated fairly by the full-service restaurants for which they work usually
explanation: Are very productive. Employees' perceptions of the way in which they are valued by their employers affect their morale, their loyalty to the full-service restaurant, and thus their productivity. These workers are loyal to the full-service restaurant and stay with it, have high morale, and have no need to file discrimination lawsuits. Their high productivity enables the full-service restaurant to be more competitive and to increase its profits.

prompt: Which of the following steps should a full-service restaurant supervisor use to aid in implementing a preventive discipline program:
choices: Maintain proper records of any infractions
Take corrective action promptly for employee's violations
explanation: Communicate standards clearly. Preventive discipline is intended to encourage full-service restaurant employees to follow standards and rules so that violations are prevented. In order to implement a preventive discipline program successfully, full-service restaurant supervisors should develop programs to control absences and grievances, involve employees in setting standards, communicate standards clearly, encourage workers to meet standards, and provide training programs in self-discipline. The other alternatives are examples of actions that could be used with corrective discipline: an approach to managing people that is intended to discourage further violations after infractions have already occurred.

prompt: An example of a benefit of a marketing-information management system is that marketers
choices: receive information that is not timely.
gain a broad perspective of the market.
obtain a collection of inappropriate data.
explanation: Gain a broad perspective of the market. Since the scope of marketing has become wider and more complicated, a greater variety of information is needed to make faster decisions. A marketing-information management system provides improved planning, organized information, and a better picture of overall marketing activities. A collection of inappropriate data that are scattered and out of date has no value to a business.

prompt: The checking method in which a list of the contents of a shipment is made on a blank invoice form is called a __________ check.
explanation: Blind. A direct check involves comparing a shipment's contents directly with the original invoice. A spot check is a random check of a few packages. In a bulk check, the contents of packages are not checked, but a count is made of the number of packages within a shipment.

prompt: One reason why owners conduct location feasibility studies before opening a new full-service restaurant is to determine if the site
choices: is in an area that has architectural controls.
will be appealing to a wide variety of vendors.
will generate the appropriate amount of business.
is adjacent to a large distribution facility.
explanation: Will generate the appropriate amount of business. A location feasibility study involves analyzing various factors that affect whether a new site will generate the appropriate amount of business. Full-service restaurants want to make sure that there are enough potential customers in the area to support a new store. Therefore, a full-service restaurant might consider the volume of vehicular and pedestrian traffic, the number of people who live in the area, the number of people who work in the area but live elsewhere, the convenience of the site, and the level of competition. All these factors affect the feasibility of a site. When conducting location feasibility studies, full-service restaurant owners usually do not consider the location of distribution facilities or if the site appeals to a wide variety of vendors. An area that has architectural controls means that the style and facade of the building must meet certain standards. This usually is not a factor in location feasibility.

prompt: Marketing strategies help full-service restaurant suppliers to achieve their goals by developing marketing
explanation: Plans. In order to be successful, full-service restaurant suppliers must have goals they want to attain and strategies, or plans, to meet those goals. These plans must be analyzed and evaluated constantly in order to meet the ever-changing needs of consumers. Profits are the monies retained by full-service restaurant suppliers, and they are major incentives for developing viable strategies. Technology is scientific applications to business objectives or the methods used to attain those objectives.

prompt: Reinhart's Restaurant Supply has determined that it will focus its marketing efforts on family-oriented, full-service restaurants. Reinhart's is engaged in __________ marketing.
explanation: Target. The identification and selection of markets for a business or for a product is known as target marketing. In order for restaurant suppliers to satisfy their customers, they need to determine who the market is for their products. Restaurant suppliers use target marketing in order to plan effective marketing activities that will reduce marketing risk. Mass marketing is designing products and directing marketing activities in order to appeal to the whole market. Frequency marketing is a fictitious term.

prompt: Full-service restaurant chains identify market segments by dividing consumers into groups that have
explanation: Similar characteristics. Market segmentation is the division of a total market into smaller, more specific groups. The basis of the division is similar characteristics that are geographic, demographic, or psychographic in nature. Some of the groups or segments have unusual interests, but not all of them do. Most people have financial needs, so this characteristic is too broad to consider for market segmentation purposes. When dividing a group by psychographics, the segment has similar rather than inconsistent values.

prompt: What is one factor that Hartman's Family Restaurant should consider when identifying promotional activities to include in its marketing plan?
explanation: Costs involved. An important part of a marketing plan is the promotional activities that a full-service restaurant will use to inform, persuade, or remind customers of its products. When identifying these activities, Hartman's Family Restaurant should consider the costs involved because it has only a certain amount of money to spend on promotion. The full-service restaurant wants to select the promotional activities that will reach the greatest number of potential customers for the most reasonable price. A marketing plan is concerned with promotional activities rather than safety issues, the inventory system, or wage regulations. However, these factors are an important part of the overall business plan.

prompt: What does a full-service restaurant try to identify as a result of conducting a situational analysis?
explanation: Threats and opportunities. One of the purposes of conducting a situational analysis is to identify the threats and opportunities in the business environment. The changing nature of the business environment brings with it many opportunities for full-service restaurants as well as potential threats. For example, a change in customers' eating habits might present an opportunity for some full-service restaurants but be a threat to other full-service restaurants. In order to be prepared to take advantage of the opportunities or deal with the threats, a full-service restaurant must first analyze the environment to find out exactly what those opportunities or threats are. A full-service restaurant does not conduct a situational analysis to identify profits and losses, revenues and expenses, or goods and services.

prompt: What is a potential strength that a full-service restaurant manager might identify in a SWOT analysis?
explanation: Market leadership. Market leadership is a potential strength that a full-service restaurant manager might identify as a result of conducting a SWOT (strengths, weaknesses, opportunities, threats) analysis. New foreign markets is an example of a potential opportunity. Large inventories is an example of a potential weakness. Market saturation is an example of a potential threat.

prompt: Which of the following is a reason why many full-service restaurant chains assess global trends and opportunities:
explanation: To enter the international market. Before full-service restaurant chains decide to enter the international market, they assess global trends and opportunities to make sure there is a market for their restaurants in other countries. Full-service restaurant chains want to find out if foreign countries have prosperous economies which will allow citizens to frequent their restaurants. They also want to find out what consumers in other countries want and need. Once they assess the situation, full-service restaurant chains can decide if they will be successful in the international market. Once full-service restaurant chains make the decision to enter the international market, they might set up shipping routes, locate warehouse space, and identify foreign intermediaries.

prompt: Which of the following describes appropriate action for a restaurant-supply business to take in planning how far ahead to predict its sales:
choices: Using a long-term sales forecast when merging with a former competitor
Using a short-term sales forecast when product demand is steady
Using a long-term sales forecast when entering a new market
Using a short-term sales forecast when there is a cash flow problem
explanation: Using a short-term sales forecast when there is a cash flow problem. Factors affecting how far ahead a restaurant-supply business needs to predict its sales include the objectives of the business, the business's resources, the purpose(s) of the forecast, and the conditions of the market. When demand for products is steady, a restaurant-supply business should probably consider a long-term forecast. When a restaurant-supply business is planning changes such as mergers and new-market entries, the restaurant-supply business will probably be better served if it uses a short-term forecast that could be more easily adjusted to the restaurant-supply business's changing environment than could a long-term forecast.

prompt: What does a full-service restaurant need to consider when developing a marketing budget?
choices: Value of spending money on advertising
explanation: Cost of performing marketing activities. Full-service restaurants need to develop budgets to set aside the funds that will be needed to perform marketing activities. Before they can develop budgets, they need to determine the cost of performing those marketing activities. For example, full-service restaurants need to consider wages paid to employees and the cost of buying supplies. Once a full-service restaurant calculates all the costs involved, it can develop a budget to fund the marketing activity. It is not effective to develop marketing activities without setting a budget to pay for the activities. Full-service restaurants do not consider forecasts of future sales figures, value of spending money on advertising, or the expense associated with offering credit when developing a marketing budget.

prompt: A restaurant-supply company currently has 1,750 customers and develops a marketing plan to increase that number by 4% this year and 5% next year. If the plan is successful, how many customers will the restaurant-supply company have by the end of next year?
explanation: 1,911. One of the objectives of a marketing plan often is to attract more customers, which leads to an increase in sales and revenue. When preparing its marketing plan, a restaurant-supply company develops specific objectives to follow that should be clear and measurable, such as increasing the number of customers by 4% this year and 5% next year. To determine the number of customers the restaurant-supply company will have by the end of next year if the marketing plan is successful, first determine the number of customers the restaurant-supply company will have this year by multiplying the current number of customers by the planned increase (1,750 x 4% or .04 = 70). Add the new customers to the number of current customers (1,750 + 70 = 1,820). To determine the increase for the next year, multiply this year's customers by the planned increase (1,820 x 5% or .05 = 91) and add the increase to the number of customers (1,820 + 91 = 1,911).

prompt: A full-service restaurant that examines all aspects of its marketing effort with the intention of identifying problems and ways to improve its performance is conducting a
explanation: Marketing audit. A marketing audit is a thorough examination of all aspects of a full-service restaurant's marketing effort, including objectives, strategies, and activities. The goal of the marketing audit is to identify problems or techniques that are working effectively with the intention of making adjustments to improve the full-service restaurant's marketing performance. A random check is a method of checking goods that involves checking a few items or containers chosen at random. A trend analysis involves identifying the general direction in which something is moving. A corporate study involves the examination of the entire business rather than just the marketing effort.

prompt: A benefit to a full-service restaurant that uses collaborative computer software is that it enables the employees to
explanation: Share information quickly. Collaborative computer software allows many full-service restaurant employees to access and share the same business information. Some applications, such as e-mail, allow employees to instantly transmit messages and business documents to coworkers who are traveling or working in other facilities, which can facilitate a quick response. By sharing information quickly, employees can take immediate action and then proceed to work on other tasks. Full-service restaurants do not use collaborative computer software to enable employees to search the Web, prepare written reports, or develop keyboarding skills.

prompt: Many full-service restaurants have replaced the printed dessert menu with a tray of attractive desserts. What is the purpose of using a dessert tray?
choices: To encourage diners to purchase desserts
To make the server's job easier
To have desserts ready to serve
To save money on printed menus
explanation: To encourage diners to purchase desserts. When the server presents appealing desserts and points out specialties of the house, the diner is more likely to be persuaded to purchase dessert. Saving money on printed menus is not a factor because desserts usually are listed on the main menu. Carrying a tray and explaining types of desserts is more complicated for the server than handing the diners menus. Desserts on the tray are for display purposes only, and these desserts are not ready to serve.

prompt: What should full-service restaurant employees do to help safeguard cash in the registers?
choices: Observe vendors while they deliver orders
Remember to set the alarm system at night
Refuse to cooperate with possible robbers
explanation: Be alert for suspicious-looking customers. Full-service restaurants often take in a lot of cash throughout the day so it is important for employees to do their part to help safeguard the cash. One way that full-service restaurant employees can help is to be alert for suspicious looking customers. These customers may be lingering in the restaurant and waiting for a time when the cashier is busy so they will have an opportunity to take cash from the registers. If full-service restaurant employees notice suspicious-looking customers, they should pay close attention to their actions in order to safeguard the cash. Employees should cooperate with robbers so robbers will leave the restaurant quickly. Setting the alarm system at night will help to prevent burglaries. Observing vendors during the delivery process will help to prevent vendor theft.

prompt: What procedure do many restaurants tell their employees to follow during a robbery?
explanation: Obey the demands. Most robbers are interested only in obtaining cash and leaving the restaurant as quickly as possible so as not to be identified. Restaurant employees should obey the robber's demands and be cooperative in order to avoid a situation that might result in violence. The employees should consider their own personal safety first because the restaurant probably carries insurance for such events. It may be impossible for employees to call the police or activate the alarms during a robbery without putting themselves in danger. They should obey the robber's demands rather than try to hide the cash.

prompt: When evaluating sites for a full-service restaurant franchise, a restaurant owner must consider the potential consumers that do not live in the trading area. This study is called a(n)
explanation: Outshopper analysis. Many factors are considered when deciding on a restaurant site, including residential support levels, area growth potential, and competitors. An outshopper analysis evaluates the people who shop, work, play, and dine in the trading area but do not live there. This factor helps in estimating the net sales potential in the area. A cooperative evaluation is not a widely used term that is used to describe forms of site analysis in the food-service industry. Census is the number of people that live in a given area. Cluster reviews are usually called cluster evaluations. These evaluations review the number of other retailers and restaurants near the selected site.

prompt: Which of the following is an activity that will help full-service restaurants keep the working environment safe for employees:
explanation: Do preventive maintenance. Many potentially dangerous or harmful situations can be avoided if full-service restaurants routinely do preventive maintenance on equipment and machinery. If full-service restaurants check electrical equipment, examine outlets, and inspect wiring on a regular basis, they will identify potential problems and be able to make repairs before dangerous situations exist. As a result, the working environment will be safe for employees. Hiring a cleaning company, offering medical training, and purchasing liability insurance are not activities that will help full-service restaurants keep the working environment safe for employees.

prompt: Full-service restaurant cashiers can help to prevent customers from cheating the business out of cash by
choices: counting the cash in the cash drawer before their shifts begin.
using the count-back method of making change.
making certain customers sign their charge card slips.
explanation: Following the business's point-of-sale procedures. To prevent point-of-sale fraud, employees should be familiar with the types of fraud associated with credit cards, checks, and cash. Full-service restaurant cashiers should follow these steps in a consistent, step-by-step manner. Using the count-back method assures customers don't get too much or too little change. A customer's signature on a charge slip allows the full-service restaurant to collect the money from the credit card company. Counting the cash in the cash drawer before shifts begin verifies the cash on hand.

prompt: Planning the quantities of menu items to prepare is an important part of production planning because it helps to
choices: locate the resources needed for the product.
sequence the steps in the preparation process.
increase consumer demand for the product.
prevent losses to the full-service restaurant.
explanation: Prevent losses to the full-service restaurant. A full-service restaurant should try to prepare only as many food items as it needs. If menu item quantities exceed consumer demand, the full-service restaurant will lose money on unsold food items. If the full-service restaurant does not produce enough to meet consumer demand, it will lead to dissatisfied customers, which may result in lost sales. Planning menu item quantities does not help increase demand, locate resources, or sequence preparation steps.

prompt: Which of the following is a step that management can take to implement a program for the achievement of quality:
explanation: Develop a clear standard. To achieve quality in a business, management must develop a clear standard for employees to follow and then enforce the standard. Employees need to know what quality of goods they are expected to produce or what quality of service they are expected to provide to customers. Having a clear standard will give employees guidelines to follow. Then, businesses need to check regularly to make sure employees are following the standard. If the business discovers problems, it needs to take action and make corrections. Standards will differ among businesses so following the lead of competitors will not necessarily be effective. Buying expensive equipment and maintaining detailed records will not guarantee that the business achieves quality.

prompt: To determine how many menu items it must sell at a certain price to make a profit, a full-service restaurant might conduct a
explanation: Break-even analysis. The break-even point is the level of sales at which revenues equal total costs. The purpose of conducting a break-even analysis is to identify the level of sales needed to reach the break-even point at various prices. Variable-price assessment, base-cost assessment, and price-break analysis are not terms that businesses commonly use to describe the level of sales that the full-service restaurant needs to reach the break-even point at various prices.

prompt: A full-service restaurant owner often has considerable influence when negotiating facility lease terms if the
choices: real estate market is saturated or slow.
tax rate is higher than the national average.
facility owner possesses more than one property.
property is located in a prime or popular location.
explanation: Real estate market is saturated or slow. When there is an abundance of properties for rent or sale, or fewer business owners are looking for facilities to rent, there is more competition among property owners for buyers or leasers. The longer a facility is unoccupied, the more money the facility owner loses. Therefore, facility owners are often more likely to agree to potential lessee's requests (e.g., lower rent, interior painting) in order to obtain cash inflow from the rentals. Ownership of multiple properties does not necessarily mean that the property owner is willing to provide concessions during lease negotiations. Tax rates are established by governments and are not negotiable. A facility owner would probably have an easier time finding tenants for a property that is located in a popular location. Therefore, the facility owner has more influence in negotiating lease terms than the prospective tenant.

prompt: A restaurant-equipment business's employees are usually expected to perform certain housekeeping duties on a regular basis in order to
explanation: Prevent damage to the products. Most restaurant-equipment business employees are expected to do a certain amount of light housekeeping work such as dusting counters or shelves and keeping items neatly arranged. These chores keep products from getting dirty, moved, or suffering other damage. Insurance premiums are the payments made to the insurance company for business insurance. Housekeeping tasks do not indicate that the restaurant equipment business offers upscale services. Taking inventory is easier when stock is in order, but housekeeping doesn't prevent the need to count stock periodically.

prompt: Which of the following is the correct procedure to follow in listing references on a job résumé:
choices: Obtain the permission of the people whose names you use.
Put personal friends at the top of the list.
List your references with your work experience.
Use initials rather than first names.
explanation: Obtain the permission of the people whose names you use. Never give someone's name as a reference on a résumé unless you have asked the person if s/he is willing to be listed. This is not only courteous, but it gives the person time to think about what s/he should say about you if asked. References should be previous employers, instructors, or others who can verify your job skills, not personal friends who may not be able to answer questions about your skills. Initials may be used if the first name is unknown, but it is better to use the first name for the most accurate identification of the person.

prompt: One way that large, full-service restaurant chains expand operations is by
explanation: Selling franchises. One way large, full-service restaurant chains expand operations is by selling franchises that allow individuals or companies to buy the right to sell a chain's products under a licensing arrangement. The franchisees provide the funds to open and operate a new full-service restaurant. As a result, the chain has more full-service restaurants available and receives compensation from the franchisee in the form of royalties or a percentage of revenue. Today, franchises are a significant portion of the restaurant industry. Full-service restaurant chains do not expand operations by reorganizing purchasing duties, identifying suppliers, or eliminating competitors.

prompt: What is a good time-management technique to follow when conducting meetings?
explanation: Keep them brief. You cannot afford to make poor use of your time by conducting meetings that don't accomplish anything. When meetings are needed, they should be carefully planned and be as brief as possible. Meetings should not be scheduled any more often than is absolutely necessary. Socializing during meetings should be kept to a minimum. Using an agenda often helps to organize meetings and keep them brief.

prompt: When a restaurant-supply company develops a complex pricing structure that makes it hard for the full-service restaurant owner to understand, the company may be acting in a(n) __________ manner.
explanation: Unethical. Unethical means lacking morals. A restaurant-supply company that intentionally tries to confuse customers by using complex or unclear pricing is acting unethically. Because this is an unethical practice, the business is not being responsible, empathetic, or moral.

prompt: The primary reason that governments impose laws prohibiting restaurant-supply companies from engaging in predatory pricing practices is to prevent monopolies and protect
explanation: Competition. Predatory pricing is a strategy in which restaurant-supply companies price products to sell below cost for the purpose of driving their competitors out of business. If a single restaurant-supply company eliminates its competition, it creates a monopoly, which limits consumers' choices. In the United States, civil rights are basic human rights that protect the nation's citizens under the U.S. Constitution. Freedom of speech is a civil right. Laws prohibiting predatory pricing protect all legal forms of business ownership, not just corporations.

prompt: One way for the Atkins Restaurant Supply Company to accomplish its goal of selling a large volume of glassware is to charge __________ prices.
explanation: Low. One way for the restaurant supply company to increase its volume of sales is to charge low prices. The restaurant supply company will generate more total income because it sells more products. Low prices probably will attract more customers who will buy goods, thereby increasing sales and profits. Charging high prices may increase the dollar value of sales but not the volume of sales. Charging competitive or moderate prices might make it more difficult to increase the volume of sales because prices are similar to those of competitors.

prompt: A full-service restaurant chain negotiates a chain trade discount of 25/20/10 percent on a food warming unit that is list priced at $180. What is the final cost of the food warming unit to the full-service restaurant chain?
explanation: $97.20. A chain trade discount is calculated in successive order on the list price of the product. In order to determine the final cost of a product listed at $180 with a 25/20/10 chain trade discount, the business multiplies the list price by the first discount ($180 x .25 = $45). Then the business subtracts the first discount amount from the list price and multiplies that figure by the second discount ($180 – $45 = $135; $135 x .20 = $27). The business subtracts the second discount amount from the first discounted price, and multiplies that figure by the third discount ($135 – $27 = $108; $108 x .10 = $10.80). Then the business subtracts the third discount amount from the second discounted price to arrive at the final cost of the product ($108.00 – $10.80 = $97.20).

prompt: Which of the following controls such new-product considerations as warranties and safety standards:
explanation: Government regulations. Many new products must meet government standards or be produced under government guidelines. Government regulations also control some of the information that must be provided consumers, such as the nutritional content of food. Governmental regulations cover factors such as warranties, noise-emission standards for a wide range of products, mobile-home construction and safety standards, auto-emission standards for new cars, and safety packaging for many products. Stages in product life cycles are the courses that products follow in the market, including introduction, growth, maturity, and decline. Market-research studies are often used to aid product/service management in order to gather information concerning consumer needs and preferences but do not control warranties and safety standards. Product characteristics may indicate the types of warranties and safety standards that are needed but do not control them.

prompt: What is a potential benefit to a full-service restaurant chain that implements an ongoing product opportunity recognition process?
explanation: Competitive advantage. A product opportunity is a situation in which a full-service restaurant chain acts on the chance to provide a good or service to a market segment that wants and is willing to pay for the product. Because circumstances are always changing, full-service restaurant chains must develop ongoing product opportunity processes to remain competitive in the marketplace. By acting on a product opportunity, the full-service restaurant chain may provide a market with a unique product, which gives the chain a competitive advantage. The competitive advantage, or the edge achieved by offering something better than competitors, is a benefit to the full-service restaurant chain. Commercialization is the point that a product goes into full-scale production, the marketing plan is put into place, sales and service training are done, and the product's life cycle begins. Implementing a product opportunity recognition process does not strengthen a country's economy or mean that a business's goals are attainable.

prompt: When The Ultimate Steakhouse purchases fresh meats, it usually specify standards that are based on
explanation: Quality and yield. Fresh meats that full-service restaurants buy are usually graded on the basis of quality and yield. Meats that are of the highest quality and provide the most yield receive the highest grade. As the quality and yield diminish, so does the rating. These standards allow a full-service restaurant to purchase the quality of meat that their customers expect when they dine at the restaurant. Color and shape, and size and taste are often standards for fresh fruits and vegetables. Quantity and cost are often factors that supermarkets consider when purchasing eggs.

prompt: Which of the following is a true statement about the consumer-protection practices of most full-service restaurants:
choices: Full-service restaurants that protect consumers are protecting themselves.
Full-service restaurants usually win when consumers file lawsuits against them.
Full-service restaurants willingly sell unsafe products if it helps them to make a profit.
Full-service restaurants benefit from publicity even if it is about selling unsafe menu items.
explanation: Full-service restaurants that protect consumers are protecting themselves. Consumer protection is business protection. When full-service restaurants protect consumers, they are protecting themselves from financial losses caused by consumer lawsuits, government fines, and unsafe products. Full-service restaurants that follow consumer-protection practices benefit by creating a positive image of social responsibility. They earn the reputation of caring about consumers as people and not just as sources of profit. This creates customer loyalty for the full-service restaurant because it usually leads to greater profits. Negative publicity hurts a full-service restaurant's image. Lawsuits filed by consumers are an expense for the full-service restaurant and can damage the restaurant's reputation.

prompt: When evaluating customers' experiences, a full-service restaurant should keep in mind that customers are most often influenced by their interactions with the restaurant's
explanation: Employees. The way that customers experience the dining experience affects how they view the full-service restaurant. Good experiences often bring the customers back, while unpleasant experiences can prompt customers to dine at other restaurants. The ways that employees interact with customers have a major impact on the customers' experiences and their perceptions of the restaurant. Helpful, courteous, and knowledgeable employees foster good customer experiences. Employees who are indifferent, rude, and lacking in knowledge often have a negative effect on the customers' experiences. Customers do not usually interact with the full-service restaurant's suppliers, labor union, or negotiation committee.

prompt: Which of the following is a way that an Italian restaurant can determine if a menu item will fulfill its target market's needs and wants:
explanation: Ask the customers. To compete in the marketplace, a full-service restaurant must develop or find menu items that will fulfill its customers' changing needs and wants. One way to determine what the customers want is by asking them. Obtaining customer feedback is a good way for an Italian restaurant to evaluate how it is meeting its customers' wants and what it needs to do to increase customer satisfaction. Distributing promotional materials, observing workers, and developing a prospect list are not activities that necessarily help a full-service Italian restaurant identify menu items that will fulfill its customers' needs and wants.

prompt: A product line extension might help a full-service restaurant that offers a short, shallow product mix to
explanation: Attract new target markets. The product mix is the particular assortment of goods and services that a full-service restaurant offers in order to meet its market's needs and its company's goals. A full-service restaurant that has a short, shallow product mix (limited menu) offers a small amount of items within one of very few product lines. A product line is a group of related products. Adding a new product line to the product mix is called a line extension. By adding a new product line to the product mix, the full-service restaurant can attract new target markets. For example, a full-service seafood restaurant chain might add steak and chicken entrees to attract customers that don't like to eat seafood. When a full-service restaurant introduces a new product (menu) line, its expenditures may increase because it may need to increase staff, offer additional food items and ingredients, and heavily promote the new menu items. Line extensions do not always improve distribution channel relationships or reduce a full-service restaurant's liability.

prompt: Should a restaurant supplier attempt to provide services to satisfy every possible customer?
choices: No, service levels aren't that important to most customers.
Yes, the loss of a prospect is a catastrophe.
No, some people make impossible demands.
Yes, this helps to maintain the desired profit margin.
explanation: No, some people make impossible demands. Although service levels may be important to many customers, satisfaction levels and expectations also vary among customers, so an attempt to satisfy every customer would be both costly and futile. The loss of a single prospect is seldom a catastrophe. Services should be offered if they are needed and serve a purpose within the restaurant supplier's philosophy, policies, and procedures. The goal of the restaurant supplier is to offer services that will satisfy the majority of its present and potential customers.

prompt: Is it possible for a brand to be harmful to a corporation of full-service restaurants?
choices: No, brands are not a negative influence on a firm.
Yes, an unsuccessful brand can harm a corporation's image.
No, consumers do not connect the brand with the corporation.
Yes, successful brands cause a corporation's other brands to fail.
explanation: Yes, an unsuccessful brand can harm a corporation's image. This occurs because consumers associate a failing brand with other brands owned by the same corporation. These consumers may view the corporation in a negative way, lose confidence in the corporation, and resist buying any of its brands in the future.

prompt: What does a full-service restaurant need to define and write out before building its brand?
explanation: Core values. The first step that a full-service restaurant takes to build and protect its brand is to define and write out core values. Core values are what a full-service restaurant stands for and what it strives to do. They are what the full-service restaurant must be. Writing down the core values helps a full-service restaurant to crystallize its thoughts and gives the values themselves added importance. Once a full-service restaurant has defined its core values, it can develop how it will deliver those values to meet customers' expectations. A full-service restaurant must define its core values before it can develop a unique name or develop guidelines for employees to follow.

prompt: Imagine that you work for a restaurant-supply distributor. Your department has an average inventory of 60 pans for the year, and your records show a total of 240 pans sold for the year. What is your stock turnover rate?
explanation: 4. Stock turnover rate is determined by dividing your average inventory into the number of units sold. In this case, 240 ÷ 60 = 4. This indicates that your department completely sold its inventory of pans four times during the year.

prompt: The Margalis Bistro decided to use a combination, or blend, of marketing communication channels to send messages to its customers about a new menu selection. The Margalis Bistro is using
explanation: A promotional mix. Promotional mix is known as the combination, or blend, of marketing communication channels that a full-service restaurant uses to send its message to customers. Personalized communication refers to messages that directly address a specific customer or consumer. Marketing strategies are plans of action for achieving marketing goals and objectives. Communication techniques include telephone, fax, letters, e-mail, and other methods of communicating messages.

prompt: A primary reason why television stations discontinue running some commercials is because consumers and advocacy groups complain that the ads are
explanation: Offensive. Consumers are exposed to hundreds of promotional messages every day. Marketers face the challenge of developing messages that consumers will remember. So consumers will remember certain products, some marketers "push the limits" by developing controversial commercials that consumers may find offensive or distasteful. Advocacy groups may complain to the government, media, and businesses about the commercials in order to pressure television stations to stop running them. Commercials may be pessimistic, sarcastic, and audible; but advocacy groups and consumers do not always find these characteristics offensive.

prompt: Which of the following is a popular promotional method used by many full-service restaurants that is sent to their customers' homes or businesses:
explanation: Direct mail. Direct mail is a promotional medium that comes to consumers' homes in the form of letters, catalogs, postcards, and folders. Many full-service restaurants prefer to use direct mail because it allows them to promote their products to a specific target market. Full-service restaurants are able to control the cost of direct mail promotions by sending literature only to current or prospective customers. A billboard is a type of outdoor advertising in which large signs are placed in prominent locations, often along highways. Rebates are a return of part of the price a customer pays for a good or service and usually are offered by the product's manufacturer. Inside posters are signs placed within the store.

prompt: Once the appropriate supplies and decorations are assembled to decorate a full-service restaurant for a special event, they must be
choices: tried out in several different arrangements.
explanation: Securely fastened in place. Making sure that decorations are securely fastened in place is necessary so that the decorations will remain effective and to prevent any part of them from falling or creating a safety problem. The effectiveness of the decorations cannot be judged until they have been in place for a period of time. The way in which the decorations are to be arranged should be decided in advance so that time is not wasted in trying out different arrangements to get the best effect. It is not necessary to get the approval of the wait staff.

prompt: Full-service restaurants use visual-merchandising techniques in order to present their menu items in such a way that customers will be persuaded to
explanation: Make purchases. The purpose of visual merchandising is to display a full-service restaurant's menu items in such a way that customers will be persuaded to purchase the items. Some full-service restaurants often display their desserts in display cases to entice customers to purchase dessert after the meal or to purchase an entire pie or cake to take home with them after dining in the restaurant. The use of visual displays supports the merchandising effort, which is the process of having the right items in the right place at the right time in order to make a profit. The ultimate goal of both merchandising and visual merchandising is to sell products. Visual merchandising is not used to persuade customers to apply for jobs, to compliment the staff, or to take photographs.

prompt: When preparing a promotional plan, which of the following types of analysis would a full-service restaurant use to obtain information about the competition:
explanation: External. An external analysis is an examination of what is occurring outside the full-service restaurant. It examines not only the full-service restaurant's target market but also the competition. The information gathered in the external analysis helps the full-service restaurant to prepare a promotional plan that will appeal to current and potential customers and make the full-service restaurant competitive. An internal analysis is an examination of what is occurring within the full-service restaurant. Personal and regional are not types of analysis used in developing promotional plans.

prompt: Which of the following is an example of a full-service restaurant coordinating its promotional activities:
choices: Seasonal menu items advertised on television are featured on the restaurant's table tents.
A pasta manufacturer and an Italian restaurant share advertising costs.
Frequent restaurant customers receive a free dessert after seven dinner purchases.
A Mexican restaurant places the same advertisement in magazines and newspapers.
explanation: Seasonal menu items advertised on television are featured on the restaurant's table tents. Promotional activities are coordinated when two or more different types of activities, such as advertising and display, are combined in order to achieve a goal. Cooperative advertising occurs when advertising costs are shared by members of the distribution channel. Using a loyalty program and placing an advertisement in two media are each examples of only one type of promotional activity.

prompt: An upscale, full-service restaurant that focuses its selling efforts on satisfying the needs and wants of its clientele is a __________ business.
explanation: Customer-oriented. Many businesses, including upscale full-service restaurants, stress to employees that the customer is always right. A service-oriented business emphasizes its services, and a product-oriented business stresses its products. A profit-oriented business considers making a profit its first priority.

prompt: Which of the following is one way that good customer service has a positive effect on sales relationships:
explanation: Promotes repeat business. Most companies realize that repeat business is important in order to be successful. One way to promote repeat business is to provide customers with good service that builds lifetime sales relationships. Customers who are satisfied with the service they receive usually continue to do business with the company. Good service helps to create loyal customers who are less likely to be influenced by competitors. Following up with customers, offering financial assistance, and suggesting new information are methods of providing customer service.

prompt: Which of the following is a customer-relations factor that often keeps customers coming back to a family-oriented, full-service restaurant:
explanation: Goodwill. Goodwill is the positive feelings that customers have toward a business. It is an advantage that a family-oriented, full-service restaurant acquires beyond the value of its food and services and is created and maintained by good relations with customers. The location of the restaurant, its prices, and its payment options are factors that often attract customers initially; but people will not become loyal customers if the full-service restaurant doesn't create goodwill.

prompt: What technology allows restaurant-supply salespeople to develop up-to-date lists of potential customers who are interested in their specific products?
explanation: Electronic data processing. Electronic data processing allows restaurant-supply salespeople to develop computerized databases of potential customers. Restaurant-supply salespeople can prepare up-to-date lists of prospective customers who are interested in their products, or they can purchase computerized databases from companies that specialize in collecting such information. For example, many organizations maintain databases about their members that they sell to others. These computerized databases contain the members' names, addresses, and information about their interests that will help restaurant-supply salespeople decide if they are qualified prospects. Restaurant-supply salespeople often use computerized presentations to demonstrate goods and services. Direct-response advertising involves sending promotional materials through the mail. Educational seminars are not a type of technology.

prompt: A restaurant-equipment supplier's catalogs, manuals, and print advertisements are a good source of __________ information for salespeople.
explanation: Product. A great deal of product information is given in product bulletins, catalogs, manuals, and print advertisements. Salespeople who read these materials usually are able to obtain information that will help them sell restaurant-equipment products to customers. A restaurant-equipment supplier's catalog provides information that customers may use to order products. Some manuals contain information about operating policies and procedures. Print advertisements are a type of promotion.

prompt: What should restaurant servers be familiar with in order to explain the features of menu items to customers?
explanation: Ingredients. Ingredients are the various food items that are used to prepare menu dishes. Restaurant servers should be familiar with the ingredients in menu items in order to be able to explain their features to customers. Customers often ask questions about how a dish is prepared in order to decide if they will like it or if it meets their dietary needs. Servers should be familiar with the ingredients in the various dishes in order to provide that information to customers. Nutrients are the components of food that provide nourishment. Perishables are items that are capable of spoiling, decaying, or dying. Condiments are relishes, spices, or sauces used to season food.

prompt: Obtaining business and personal information about potential clients is part of the __________ phase of the selling process.
explanation: Prospecting. Prospecting is the process of identifying and locating potential clients. It enables sales representatives to tailor their sales calls to the prospects' needs. The approach is the initial contact with the customer. Reaching closure is the phase of the selling process in which the salesperson addresses customer objections and asks the customer to buy. Follow-up includes all the activities that occur after a sale to ensure customer satisfaction.

prompt: The restaurant-equipment salesperson should pause before answering a customer's objections in order to
choices: let the customer see that s/he is upset.
explanation: Get the customer's full attention. The restaurant-equipment salesperson should not rush to answer customers' objections, but s/he should not delay dealing with the objection. Instead, s/he should make sure the customer has finished, pause for a minute, collect his/her thoughts, and then respond calmly and quietly. This helps to show the customer that the restaurant-equipment salesperson is not upset about the objection. Showing empathy for customers involves letting them know that you understand their point of view.

prompt: When a full-service restaurant prepares salads for customers, when should the restaurant add the salad dressings?
explanation: Just prior to serving. Salad dressings should be added to salads just prior to serving to avoid wilting the salads. Dressings add moisture to salads, which causes wilting. By adding the dressings just prior to serving, the salads will be fresh and attractive. Some full-service restaurants prepare salads in advance and refrigerate them until they are served. However, dressings should not be added before refrigerating because that will lead to wilting. Dressings should be added after combining ingredients only if the salads will be served immediately. Full-service restaurants usually do not add dressings during the presentation.

prompt: Determine the amount of tax for a china and flatware purchase of $57.00 with a tax rate of 4%.
explanation: $2.28. The tax rate should be converted to a decimal and then multiplied by the amount of the purchase to determine the amount of tax (4% or .04 x $57.00 = $2.28).

prompt: Determine the check amount due without tax when a full-service restaurant customer is paying cash for the following menu items: 5 chicken dinners at $14.98 each; 3 cheesecake desserts at $2.50 each; 1 pork-chop entree $14.95 at each; 1 lobster dinner at $25.00 each.
explanation: $122.35. When customers buy more than a single unit of each item, multiply the unit price by the quantity. In this example, five chicken dinners are $74.90 ($14.98 x 5 = $74.90), three orders of cheesecake are $7.50 ($2.50 x 3 = $7.50), and the pork-chop entree and lobster dinner are $14.95 and $25.00 respectively. Add these prices together to determine the total amount due ($74.90 + $7.50 + $14.95 + $25.00 = $122.35).

prompt: Why do many restaurants take reservations?
explanation: To shorten wait time. Many restaurants take reservations so they will know how many customers to expect and when the customers will arrive. By taking reservations, restaurants can help customers select a time when a table will be ready so the customers do not need to wait. For example, if a restaurant seats 80 people, it might take reservations for a 6:00 or 6:30 seating and for an 8:00 or 8:30 seating. That allows for one group of customers to finish and leave before another group arrives, thereby shortening wait time. Although many restaurants take reservations, they cannot control the flow of customers who arrive without reservations. Restaurants do not take reservations to predict portion size or reduce operating expense.

prompt: The primary purpose for a server to use up-selling techniques with restaurant guests is to
explanation: Increase the check amount. Up-selling is a sales technique in which a higher priced product than the one originally requested by the guest is suggested by the server. For example, when a guest orders a breakfast platter, the server might try to up-sell the buffet by telling the guest that for only $2.00 more, the buffet has all of the items on the platter and that the guest can go to the buffet for multiple helpings. If the guest decides to order the buffet option, the check size increases. If the check size increases substantially, the server's tip may increase, too. Although up-selling a buffet option may reduce the guests' waiting time for meals, up-selling occurs in other situations in which waiting time is not a factor. Up-selling should not affect service levels, and it does not necessarily decrease food-waste ratios.

prompt: In a full-service restaurant chain, which of the following would be the responsibility of top-level management:
explanation: Accomplishing company goals. Top-level management uses the full-service restaurant chain's resources to achieve company goals through the management activities of planning, organizing, directing, and controlling. First-line supervisors have the responsibility for supervising day-to-day activities. Maintaining security and conducting research would be the responsibility of mid-level managers.

prompt: Which of the following pairs of businesses are examples of direct competitors:
explanation: Outback Steakhouse and Longhorn Restaurant. Direct competition is competition that occurs among businesses which offer similar goods or services. Outback and Longhorn are direct competitors for consumers' full-service restaurant purchases. All of the other alternatives are businesses that are in indirect competition with each other because they offer dissimilar goods or services.
